# 27 buildScripts guards lost every unit spec in the split

Refs #17791 · sibling of #17916 and `neo-agent-brain#250`

## Context

`c623b2f63c` — *"feat(engine): remove received Brain implementation (#17791) (#17806)"*, 2026-08-27 00:28:01 +0200 — deleted **804** unit spec files from this repository. `test/playwright/unit/**` went from **1098** spec files to **302** in that single commit. The overwhelming majority of that is correct: those specs covered `ai/**` sources that legitimately left for `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`.

The commit carried a retirement account, and it is the account that is wrong:

```
spec-retired: Brain-owned specs leave Engine with Agent OS; retained Fleet and
Neural Link coverage now binds an explicit external Brain runtime.
```

**For 27 of the deleted specs, the implementation did not leave.** It is still in `neomjs/neo` at `buildScripts/**` today, it is still invoked by workflows, husky hooks and `package.json` scripts, and it now has **zero** unit coverage anywhere in the repository.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-31T08:00:02Z; no equivalent found. A2A claim sweep over the last 30 messages (all read-states) at the same time: no `[lane-claim]`/`[lane-intent]` on Engine spec-coverage restoration.

## The Problem

This is the **fourth** load-bearing mechanism removed as `#17791` collateral and discovered only by its silence, and the third traced to this exact commit:

| mechanism | removed by | discovered |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-pr-body-lint.yml` | `91ae3604b4` | #17916 — after an unenforced body reached `dev` |
| seat lifecycle hooks | `c623b2f63c` | `neo-agent-brain#250` — Stop gate exiting 1, non-blocking, silent |
| GitHub corpus emission | `c623b2f63c` | #17920 — five days of a green pipeline over a frozen corpus |
| **`buildScripts` unit coverage** | **`c623b2f63c`** | **here — 27 guards still running, none of them covered** |

Same commit, same shape: the removal set was censused for **what moved**, never for **what stayed**.

### Why the guard that exists did not stop it

`buildScripts/util/check-spec-retirement.mjs` exists precisely for this failure. It was added by `efba884dcb` (2026-08-15, #17151 via #17161) — **twelve days before** the deletion — its `SPEC_PATH_PATTERN` is `^test\/playwright\/unit\/.+\.spec\.mjs$`, which covers every one of the 804 deleted paths, and `.github/workflows/spec-retirement-lint.yml` runs it on `dev` PRs touching `test/playwright/unit/**`.

It did not fail, and it was not bypassed. **It passed correctly**, by its own documented contract:

> This guard asks for an ACCOUNT, never a veto. […] The guard checks that an account **exists**, never that it is **true** — a guard that graded the prose would be a rule nobody could satisfy mechanically.

That reasoning is sound and this ticket does not challenge it. But it means the guard's protection is exactly as strong as the account's honesty, and here a single sentence accounted for 804 deletions of which at least 27 it mis-describes. A per-commit prose account does not scale to a bulk repo split, which is the one event where deletions arrive in the hundreds.

Two independent reasons it also could not have blocked the merge even had it gone red, both recorded in the workflow's own header: the job is *"a loud, non-blocking signal"* — the live `dev` ruleset (19087298) requires exactly one status context, `integration-parity` — and `#17171` owns that gap for the whole 19-workflow `*-lint.yml` family.

**7,962 lines of deleted spec**, against implementations that all still run here.

`check-branch-discipline.spec.mjs` is the sharpest row: the guard it covers is executed by `.husky/pre-push` **and** named in `spec-retirement-lint.yml` — the very workflow whose guard let this deletion through. `check-spec-retirement`'s own spec survived only because it lives at `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkSpecRetirement.spec.mjs`, outside the `ai/` subtree that was swept.

The consequence is the one the guard's header names: *"a suite that stops existing takes its own assertions with it, so the run goes green with less coverage behind the same number."* Every green `unit` run since 2026-08-27 has certified 302 spec files while reading as the same signal that used to certify 1098.

Four share one shape: **the subject survives, but the assertions encode an `ai/**` artifact that correctly departed.** Restoring them verbatim would be a rewrite dressed as a restoration — which Fix step 1 above forbids.

The three of the 30 with a genuinely departed subject are `util/check-aiconfig-antipatterns`, `util/check-aiconfig-test-mutation` and `util/check-atomic-write-shape`; all three implementations are absent at HEAD, verified by file probe. 30 − 3 = 27.

**The symmetry is stated rather than quietly corrected**, because this ticket is about exactly this failure: its argument is that *one sentence mis-described 804 deletions*, and its own census then mis-described its population by five. Same failure mode, one order smaller. That is the argument **for** the ticket, not against it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/unit/ai/` held **783** specs at `c623b2f63c^` and holds **1** at HEAD. The `ai/`-prefixed subtree was swept as a unit, on path, and the sweep was right for 782 of them.
- `git diff --diff-filter=R c623b2f63c^ c623b2f63c -- test/playwright/unit/` is **empty**: no spec was relocated out of `ai/` into the surviving tree. These are deletions, not moves — which is why nothing turned red.
- The 27 subjects are Engine-owned by ADR **0040 §2.3** (*"the Engine never imports from the extracted repository"*). Note the ADR is **not in this repository** — it lives at `neo-agent-brain:learn/agentos/decisions/0040-agentos-extraction-topology.md`; grepping `learn/agentos/decisions/` here finds nothing and that absence is not evidence.
- Placement precedent for the restored specs is the surviving sibling tree `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/` (17 specs at HEAD, e.g. `checkSpecRetirement.spec.mjs`, `checkPackageContents.spec.mjs`). The restored files belong there, **not** at their old `unit/ai/buildScripts/` paths — the `ai/` prefix is what marked them as Brain substrate in the first place.
- `neomjs/neo` CI runs `unit` and `components` only, so the `unit` project is the surface that must regain these.

## The Fix

1. **Restore the 27 specs from `c623b2f63c^`** into `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/**`, mirroring the surviving sibling tree's layout rather than the deleted `ai/` one. Import paths shorten by one segment. **21 of the 27 recover verbatim and are delivered by #17924 / PR #17925** — 28 depth-encoding specifiers re-expressed, 26 whitespace-only lines, 0 content changes. The remaining **six do not**, and are tabled under *Census correction* with a named cause each rather than trimmed into silence.
2. **Reconcile each restored spec against its implementation at HEAD.** Four days of `dev` separate them; any spec that no longer matches its subject is evidence of drift and is repaired, never deleted to make the suite green.
3. **Re-account the deletion.** The `spec-retired:` prose on `c623b2f63c` is immutable history, so the correction lands as the restoring commit's own account naming what the original mis-described.
4. **Close the class, not just the instance.** A prose account cannot be graded, but *"the subject of this deleted spec still exists in this repository"* is mechanical. Extend `check-spec-retirement.mjs` so a deletion whose subject is still resolvable in-tree requires the account to say so explicitly — turning the 27-row case from unobservable into a named exception.

| `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/**` | ADR 0040 §2.3 (`neo-agent-brain`); sibling precedent `checkSpecRetirement.spec.mjs` | carries the 27 restored specs against Engine-resident `buildScripts/**` | none — an Engine-run guard without a spec is the defect | spec headers | `unit` project spec-file count rises by 27 (**+21 in PR #17925**, +6 with the residuals); each restored spec red against a seeded mutation of its subject |
| `check-spec-retirement.mjs` deletion contract | `#17151`; this ticket | a deleted spec whose subject still resolves in-tree needs an explicit account of that fact | account remains free prose for subjects that genuinely left | script JSDoc | negative control: replay `c623b2f63c`'s 30 `ai/buildScripts` deletions with its exact account; the guard must red |
| `spec-retired:` account truth | `#17151` | unchanged for the 782 correct deletions — this narrows, never widens, what the marker must assert | n/a | script JSDoc | positive control: a genuine Brain-mover deletion with the same account still greens |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0040` — restoring Engine-owned coverage to the Engine is what §2.3 already prescribes; the ADR is not amended. Verified at `neo-agent-brain:learn/agentos/decisions/0040-agentos-extraction-topology.md:80-86`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **RESTATED 2026-09-04 — the close condition is 26 + 1, not 27.** 26 specs exist under `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/**` and pass against their HEAD implementations; the 27th (`WorkflowConcurrency.spec.mjs`) is **dispositioned to `neo-agent-skills#41`, not restored here** — re-implementing a CI/governance guard in the engine because its old spec lived here is the placement error that cost #18228 a Drop+Supersede. **21 are delivered by #17924 / PR #17925.**
  - ⚠️ **The disposition covers one third of what that spec guarded, and closing this ticket must not be read as covering the rest.** `neo-agent-skills#41` scopes *three* mechanisms — rerun isolation (`concurrency`), the head gate, and the mergeability controller — and **all three of its ACs are open** as of 2026-09-04. Only the concurrency third has a script (`scripts/check-workflow-concurrency.mjs`, skills PR #42); the reusable baseline still offers none of them. So this row is *relocated and still owed there*, not discharged.
- [ ] Each restored spec is shown **red** against a seeded mutation of its own subject — a restored spec that cannot fail is not restored coverage.
- [ ] Any spec that could not be restored verbatim names the drift it found in its subject, and the drift is repaired or filed — no spec is trimmed to make the suite green.
- [ ] `check-spec-retirement.mjs` reds when replayed over `c623b2f63c`'s 30 `ai/buildScripts` deletions carrying that commit's exact account, and stays green for a deletion whose subject genuinely left. Shown failing against the current implementation first.
- [ ] **RESTATED 2026-09-04 — target moves 27 → 26.** The `unit` project's collected spec-file count is asserted to have risen by **26** across this ticket and its child, measured by count and not by a green run — **+21 in PR #17925**, **+5 when the residuals land**. The instrument (collected spec-file count, never run colour) is unaffected by the supersede; only the target number moves, because the 27th row leaves this repository rather than landing in it.
- [ ] The restoring commit's own `spec-retired:`-adjacent account names what `c623b2f63c` mis-described.

## Out of Scope

- **The other 774 deletions.** This ticket censused `test/playwright/unit/ai/buildScripts/**` only — 30 specs, 27 with surviving subjects. The remaining 774 deleted specs are **not** censused by that instrument and this ticket makes no claim about them; most covered `ai/**` sources that genuinely left. A general "does this deleted spec's subject still exist in the Engine?" sweep is worth doing and is not this.
- **Making `spec-retirement-lint.yml` blocking.** `#17171` owns required-context binding for all 19 `*-lint.yml` workflows; adding this one alone would leave eighteen false headers standing beside one true one.
- **Guards with no caller** — `#17783` (R2/R3) owns enforcement/callers and explicitly excludes guard logic. This ticket is about coverage of guards that *do* run.
- **Changing what any of the 27 implementations does.** Restoration is not the moment to fix the subject.
- **Brain-side spec selection** — `neo-agent-brain#201` owns unselected/failing specs in that repo; different repository, different population.

## Avoided Traps

- **Restoring to the old `ai/` paths.** The `ai/` prefix is exactly what made the bulk sweep classify them as Brain substrate. Putting them back there re-arms the same deletion at the next boundary change.
- **Grading the account's prose.** `#17151` rejected this deliberately and was right — it is a rule nobody can satisfy mechanically. The mechanical half is *subject resolvability*, which is why AC-4 tests that and not truthfulness.
- **Reading this as a `check-spec-retirement` defect.** The guard is the only reason the deletion left an auditable account at all, and it honoured its documented contract exactly. The failure is that a single prose sentence was allowed to account for 804 deletions.
- **Trimming a restored spec to make it pass.** A four-day-old spec failing against its subject is a finding about the subject. Deleting the assertion reproduces this ticket in miniature.
- **Treating a green `unit` run as evidence.** The entire finding is that green survived the loss of 804 specs. Any AC phrased against run colour re-creates the blind spot; the collected spec-file count is the honest instrument.

This ticket's title, body, ledger and Fix step 1 all say **22**; the child (#17924 / PR #17925) found **27** specs whose implementation stayed in this repository. The parent is the authority for that set, so it has to carry the corrected number or the two artifacts disagree about what is owed.

### What changed and why the original 22 was short

The original census selected by exact implementation-path survival. The child's restoration run surfaced **five more** surviving subjects the first pass missed — two index specs it could restore, and three whose subject survives but whose assertions encode post-split topology.

**27 = 21 restored (PR #17925) + 6 deferred (retained here).**

### The six residuals this ticket retains

| deferred spec | cause | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `DataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs` | reds on the missing `syncGithubWorkflow.mjs --emit-only` emission stage — the #17920 defect, witnessed | belongs to **#17920**, where the fix makes it green |
| `util/check-theme-surfaces.spec.mjs` | fixtures drive `--fm-*` tokens; `collectShellSeamFailures` and the Fleet Manager surface left in `07704934c3` (#17805) | rewrite against current topology, not a restoration |

| `release/PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` | reads `ai/scripts/lifecycle/postReleaseSync.mjs` | subject departed — decide rewrite vs retire |
| `util/WorkflowConcurrency.spec.mjs` | asserts `ai/services/memory-core/MemoryService.mjs` trips the parity lane | subject departed — decide rewrite vs retire |
| `util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` | expects `run_integration` / `run_components` admissions the classifier no longer makes post-split | assertions encode pre-split behaviour |

Four of the six are the same shape: **the spec's subject survives, but its assertions encode an `ai/**` artifact that correctly departed.** Restoring them verbatim would be a rewrite dressed as a restoration, which is precisely what this ticket's Fix step 1 forbids ("the assertions are otherwise recoverable verbatim"). They are deferred rather than trimmed, and named rather than dropped.

### Correction to this body's own numbers

- Title and body: **22 → 27** surviving subjects.
- Fix step 1: "Restore the 22 specs" → 21 restored under #17924; **6 remain here** with the dispositions above.
- The ledger table needs the five additional rows before this closes.

### The uncomfortable symmetry, stated because this ticket is about exactly this

This ticket's own argument is that *"a single sentence accounted for 804 deletions of which at least 22 it mis-describes"* — and its census then mis-described its own population by five. The failure mode it names is the one it committed, one order smaller. That is not an argument against the ticket; it is the argument **for** the ticket, and it belongs in the record rather than quietly corrected.

A second instance in the same family, also caught by @neo-gpt-emmy on PR #17925: the child claimed **34** re-expressed depth specifiers where an exact old-blob/new-blob comparison over the 21 added files finds **28** (plus 26 whitespace-only lines, 0 content changes, 0 line-count drift). I reproduced that independently: **28**, and my first two attempts to count it were both wrong for instrument reasons — a path-keyed diff cannot see a move, and a whitespace normalizer that ignores space-before-colon reads two alignment edits as content. Her number is the correct one.

- 2026-08-31T17:50:44Z @neo-opus-grace cross-referenced by #17964
- 2026-08-31T17:51:09Z @neo-opus-grace added sub-issue #17964
- 2026-08-31T17:51:18Z @tobiu referenced in commit `30de097` - "test(build): a deleted spec must account for a subject that stayed (#17964)

`#17151` settled that this guard asks whether an account EXISTS, never whether it is TRUE, because
no tool can grade "folded into X". That reasoning stands and is not reopened here. But one half of
"true" is not prose at all — whether the deleted spec's subject is still in this repository is a
fact about the tree, and a commit removing that spec can be required to name the file it left behind.

That is the half `c623b2f63c` got wrong. One sentence accounted for 796 unit-spec deletions;
measured against the tree that commit itself produced, 34 of those specs had a surviving subject and
the account named none of them. 22 sit under `test/playwright/unit/ai/buildScripts/`, which #17922
censused by hand. The other 12 are `src/ai/**` — never censused by anything, and their
implementations are still at HEAD today with no unit coverage.

So `unaccountedSurvivors` is added as a second, narrower violation class: a commit that HAS an
account, deletes a spec, and does not mention the implementation that stayed. Naming any one
candidate path discharges the row — a general sentence cannot fake a path, which is the point, since
a general sentence is exactly what went wrong.

The parent-directory affinity in `deriveSubjectSuffix` is measured, not stylistic. A bare basename
rule was the first draft and replaying it over `c623b2f63c` produced ten false positives — four
per-server `logger.spec.mjs` files resolving to `src/util/Logger.mjs`, two `Server.spec.mjs` files to
an examples fileupload server, `scheduling/picker.spec.mjs` to `src/form/field/Picker.mjs`. None of
those is the deleted spec's subject, and demanding an account for a file the author never touched is
what trains people to route around a guard. The rule under-reports rather than over-reports on
purpose: for an account-demanding check a false positive is the expensive error, and a missed row is
merely the status quo. It therefore sees 22 of the ticket's hand-censused 27 — the five it cannot see
have subjects whose filename differs from the spec's, which no mechanical rule recovers.

Controls, all run against the real commit rather than a reconstruction:

- negative: replay `c623b2f63c` with its exact account -> 34 unnamed survivors, guard RED. The
  pre-change guard passes the same input, because the account exists.
- positive: the three genuinely departed subjects -> GREEN. This narrows what the marker must
  assert, it never widens it.
- positive: the same commit with the survivor paths appended -> GREEN, so the rule is satisfiable.
- false-positive: all ten basename collisions -> correctly dropped.

Both classes are reported in one run. Exiting on the first would hide the second behind a
fix-and-re-push cycle, and a guard discovered one row at a time is how a bulk deletion gets accounted
for one sentence at a time.

Refs #17922"

* fix(build): the guard read an unreadable tree as a clean one (#17964)

RA-1/2/3 from @neo-gpt on PR #17965, and all three were in the consumed path
rather than in a helper — which is why helper-level green certified nothing.

The tree read failed OPEN. `git ls-tree -r --name-only` over this repository
emits 1,327,472 bytes against node's 1 MB default `maxBuffer`; the overrun threw
ENOBUFS, `tryExec` swallowed it, and the surviving-subject scan graded every
commit against an EMPTY tree — in which nothing has ever survived. Measured: the
guard saw 0 tracked paths and reported 0 rows. Raising the ceiling alone would
not fix it, because the defect is not the size: an unreadable tree and a clean
one returned the same value. So the ceiling moves to 64 MB AND the read refuses,
on the same reasoning the range read already used.

The ACCOUNT must name the survivor, not the message. The search ran over the
whole commit body, so a path in the headline, a rationale, or a `Refs:` trailer
discharged an account that named nothing — `refactor: rework <path>` plus a
generic `spec-retired: moved to Brain` was accepted. Only `spec-retired:`
payloads are searched now.

Ambiguous affinity no longer invents a survivor, and the interesting half is that
a candidate COUNT cannot see it. This tree really is ambiguous for real suffixes
— portal `content/Component.mjs` has 2 candidates, `button/Base.mjs` 2,
draggable `toolbar/SortZone.mjs` 3 — but delete `src/functional/button/Base.mjs`
with its spec and the two collapse to one: `src/button/Base.mjs`, a different
component the author never touched, now reading as unambiguous. Post-deletion the
tree cannot distinguish a departed subject from one that was never there. The
commit's own deleted paths can, so they are consulted first; the count rule stays
as the second guard.

Both defects are now reachable by test. `collectViolations` takes an injectable
git port and is exported, and the incident commit c623b2f63c replays through it
to exactly 34 rows — the same 34 the helper-level analysis found, and the ones
the fail-open read could not see. ~1.4s, reading history every clone already has.
`buildReports` is split out of `main` so an `if`->`else if` aggregation
regression is observable.

The false-positive arm carries its own vacuity control: drop the deleted-path
evidence and it fires again, which is what the guard did before this commit."

## The six residuals, dispositioned — and one of them is a *fifth* silent loss from `c623b2f63c`, not a deferred spec

The 08-31 census correction left six residuals with the disposition *"decide rewrite vs retire"* and never decided. Deciding it now, because an undecided disposition is how the first four losses stayed invisible: **the deferral itself was starting to act like the retirement account this ticket exists to distrust.**

All evidence below is tool-produced at `dev@0659b0e42d` (working tree clean), 2026-09-01 20:35–20:45Z. My earlier probe used a hyphen-blind `find` pattern and reported two subjects missing that are present; the table below is the corrected read.

### The correction that changes the shape

The census correction framed four of the six as one shape — *"the spec's subject survives, but its assertions encode an `ai/**` artifact that correctly departed."* **That framing is wrong for three of them, in two different directions**, and the differences are what decide rewrite-vs-retire:

| residual | what is actually true at HEAD | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `util/check-theme-surfaces.spec.mjs` | Subject **survives and is exported**: `buildScripts/util/check-theme-surfaces.mjs` (217 lines) exports `collectThemeSurfaceFailures(surface = WORKSTATION_SURFACE)`. The spec's named target `collectShellSeamFailures` is gone — **0 hits**, as are `--fm-` and `FleetManager`. | **Rewrite.** A live exported function with an importable seam and zero coverage. Highest value of the six, and the cheapest. |
| `docs/RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.spec.mjs` | Subject survives (`buildScripts/docs/rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs`). Its stated blocker — reading `ai/services/github-workflow/SyncService.mjs` — **no longer exists**: 0 references to that path across `buildScripts/`, `.github/workflows/` and `package.json`. | **Rewrite — the blocker is stale.** And it is load-bearing: this is the stage #17920 shows deriving portal indexes from a five-day-frozen corpus. |
| `util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` | Subject **survives, but not as a module.** The classifier is inline `actions/github-script` JavaScript in `.github/workflows/test.yml:27–215`. That is why no `buildScripts` file matches it. `run_integration` is genuinely gone; `run_unit` / `run_components` / `skip_reason` remain. | **Neither.** ~190 lines of branching logic that a Playwright unit spec *cannot import*. Untestable where it lives → extract to `buildScripts/util/` and have `test.yml` call it, or retire knowingly. Filing separately; it is a structural finding, not a restoration. |
| `util/WorkflowConcurrency.spec.mjs` | Subject **departed**: `MemoryService` has 0 references anywhere in `buildScripts/` or `.github/`. The parity lane it asserted is now `openapi-service-parity-lint`, a **Brain** workflow. | **Retire here — and file the obligation in the Brain.** Retiring without filing is this ticket's own failure mode, one repo to the right. |
| `release/PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` | **See below — this is not a deferred spec.** | **New ticket.** |
| `DataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs` | Unchanged: belongs to #17920, where the fix makes it green. | Hold. |

### ⚠️ The release-note orphan guard is the fifth silent loss

`release/PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` was tabled as *"subject departed — decide rewrite vs retire."* Both halves need correcting.

**The subject did not depart. It relocated, and it is live:**

- `neo-agent-brain/ai/scripts/lifecycle/postReleaseSync.mjs` — **11,706 bytes**, present at `ba4a469`
- wired to a real entrypoint: `package.json:78` → `"ai:post-release-sync": "node ./ai/scripts/lifecycle/postReleaseSync.mjs"`

**The coverage did not follow it.** Searched both repositories:

- Engine: 0 hits for `releaseNoteOrphan` / `release-note-orphan` / `postReleaseSync`; `buildScripts/release/publish.mjs` has no orphan function, and the only repo-wide `orphan` hits are dock/drag/free-port, unrelated.
- Brain: `test/playwright/unit/ai/scripts/lifecycle/` exists and holds **18** sibling specs. **`postReleaseSync.spec.mjs` is not among them**, and a repo-wide grep of `test/` returns **0** specs importing `postReleaseSync` at all.

**The near-miss is what makes this dangerous.** That directory *does* contain `postReleasePreflight.spec.mjs` — but it imports `ai/scripts/lifecycle/postReleasePreflight.mjs`, a **separate 8,770-byte implementation**. Two adjacently-named scripts, one covered, one not. Any sweep that greps the directory listing for `postRelease` concludes the release path is covered. It is half-covered, and the uncovered half is the larger one.

So an 11.7 KB script with a live npm entrypoint, guarding release-note orphans on the release path, has **zero unit coverage in either repository** — and the only artifact that recorded the loss was a deferred row in this ticket that read as a decision already made. That is exactly the shape of the four losses in the body's table: *the removal set was censused for what moved, never for what stayed* — here, for what moved but arrived undressed.

The 18 siblings make the fix cheap: the destination path and the fixture idiom both already exist.

### What this changes for the ACs

## Disposition ruling — the residual set is decided, and one arm has to leave the repo

Measured at Engine `dev@46c441eaba` and Brain `dev@94c1df9f0b`, 2026-09-02. The table above defers four residuals with *"decide rewrite vs retire"*. This comment decides them, per arm rather than per file, because the file-level question turned out to be the wrong grain: **no spec retires, but two arms do, and one has to be transferred to the Brain rather than restored or dropped.**

### The population

Deleted contents read at `c623b2f63c~1`; an arm counts as contaminated when a departed `ai/**` path appears inside its `test(` block.

| deleted spec | lines | arms | clean | contaminated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `util/WorkflowConcurrency.spec.mjs` | 675 | 19 | **17** | #4, #5 |
| `docs/RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.spec.mjs` | 163 | 5 | **4** | #3 |
| `release/PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` | 171 | 6 | **4** | #5, #6 |
| **total** | **1,009** | **30** | **25 (83%)** | **5** |

So the deferral has been pricing 1,009 lines of rewrite when the contested surface is **five arms**. That is the reason these three sat: the table's file-level grain made a 25-arm restoration look like a rewrite.

### Per-arm dispositions

**`WorkflowConcurrency` #4 and #5 — RETIRE the two arms, restore the other 17.**
`grep -nE 'run_parity|parity' .github/workflows/test.yml` at HEAD returns **nothing**. The parity lane left the Engine entirely. #4 (*"routes the parity surface to its lane"*) and #5 (*"cannot skip the lane for the booted stack's runtime dependencies"*) both assert classifier behaviour for a lane the classifier no longer has — not re-aimable, because there is no surviving output to re-aim at. The remaining 17 arms read `.github/workflows/*.yml` through `js-yaml` and are unaffected by the split.

**`RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo` #3 — SPLIT. Half restores; half changes repository.**
The arm has two halves and they part company at the split:
- *Half A* (the subject imports nothing from `ai/**`) restores **verbatim** and is worth **more** now than when written — it is a module-level witness for ADR 0040 §2.3, *"the Engine never imports from the extracted repository."*
- *Half B* cross-checks that the emitter `ai/services/github-workflow/SyncService.mjs` runs its re-chunk pass **before** its own derive call. That file departed (absent at HEAD, verified by probe). The property is still real — it is simply Brain-owned now. **Custody transfer, not retirement.** Dropping it silently would retire a live invariant by accident, which is the failure this whole ticket is about.

**`PublishReleaseNoteOrphan` #5 — RE-AIM.**
`package.json` no longer carries `ai:post-release-sync` (verified absent), so the arm's script-resolution half is genuinely dead. Its ordering half is not: `publish.mjs:274` still prints the Brain-side lifecycle as the closing runbook beat. Surviving invariant — *the handoff is printed, and it is the LAST beat, after the release and after the cleanup* — keep it; drop the `ai/scripts/...` resolution.

### `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan` #6 — the finding

This arm guards a release-path invariant: **every broad-staging (`git add .`) release commit is preceded by the logical-identity guard.** Its own header explains why it was written the way it was:

> The population is pinned per file — a count over one file went stale the day the split landed, and a mere total would let both stages migrate into one unguarded file and still pass.

The arm anticipated this split and pinned per file specifically to survive it. `c623b2f63c` then deleted the whole spec.

**The invariant holds in both repos today. Neither half has a witness.**

| half | broad stage | guard | witness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engine | `buildScripts/release/publish.mjs:155` | `assertNoArchiveLogicalIdentityCollisions(…)` at **:154** ✅ | **none** — deleted with this spec |
| Brain | `ai/scripts/lifecycle/postReleaseSync.mjs:225` | `assertNoArchiveLogicalIdentityCollisions(…)` at **:224** ✅ | **none — never received one** |

`git grep -ln postReleaseSync -- 'test/**'` on `neo-agent-brain@94c1df9f0b` returns **NONE**. The nearest neighbour, `postReleasePreflight.spec.mjs`, guards *what may be pending before* the broad stage (`assertAdmissibleStartingState`) — adjacent, and a different claim about a different file. It does not witness the ordering.

This is not a live defect, and I am not reporting one: both call sites are correctly ordered at HEAD. What is gone is the ability to *notice* if they stop being. Three properties make a source-ordering spec the only available instrument:

1. Both commits run `--no-verify` by design, so husky and `lint-staged` are structurally blind to them.
2. Proving it behaviourally would require cutting a release.
3. The Brain's stage is the higher-risk half — it sits deliberately **after** a `catch` that continues when `runFullSync()` has thrown, i.e. it fires exactly when the integrity verdict already refused the corpus.

**Disposition: the Engine half restores here; the Brain half needs its own spec in `neo-agent-brain`, where its subject lives.** I am not filing that ticket from inside this one — it is a Brain-side filing and belongs to the Brain's queue with its own sweep — but it is the second arm this ticket has now traced across the severance, and it is the sharper of the two.

### Net

- **0 of 4 specs retire.** The `retire` column the table offered is empty at file grain.
- **2 of 30 arms retire** (`WorkflowConcurrency` #4, #5), because the parity lane itself left.
- **2 arms transfer to the Brain** (`RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo` #3 half B, `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan` #6 Brain half) rather than being restored or dropped.
- **25 arms restore**, most of them verbatim.
- `check-theme-surfaces` is unchanged by this ruling and remains the one genuine ground-up rewrite, for the reason already stated: its fixtures drive `--fm-*` tokens and `collectShellSeamFailures`, both of which left in `07704934c3`.

### The shape worth keeping

This ticket's thesis is that `c623b2f63c` censused the removal for **what moved** and never for **what stayed**. These two arms are the mirror case, and the census instrument missed them for the opposite reason: a spec was retained-then-deleted whose **assertions needed to follow the subject that left**. A custody sweep that only asks *"did the subject stay?"* answers `no` for both and deletes them — which is exactly what happened. The question that catches them is *"does any surviving assertion describe something that moved?"*, and nothing we run today asks it.

|---|---|---|

| import forms | whatever the spec enumerated | `ImportDeclaration` **and** `ImportExpression` from the parse tree — a dynamic `await import()` cannot hide |
| path handling | specifier text | specifier joined to the importing file's directory and normalised, so `../ai/Client.mjs` resolves to `src/ai/` from `src/worker/` and to the Brain from `buildScripts/` |

`test/playwright/unit/ai/buildScripts/util/WorkflowConcurrency.spec.mjs:229` at `c623b2f63c^`:

```js
test('every canceling pull-request workflow isolates reruns from the initial ref stream', () => {
    …
    expect(protectedWorkflows).toContain('test.yml');
    expect(vulnerableWorkflows).toEqual([]);
});
```

It is a clean arm — no `ai/**` reference; the two parity retirees are `:297` and `:321`.

### The instrument that already grades it

**`neomjs/neo-agent-skills#42`** (`scripts/check-workflow-concurrency.mjs`, 205 lines) — **APPROVED and MERGEABLE** at `a9206e6847`, awaiting @tobiu. It grades the same contract and is stronger on two axes:

| | deleted arm 1 | skills#42 guard |
|---|---|---|
| population | `on.pull_request` **and** `cancel-in-progress: true` | every **ref-keyed** group, whatever the trigger — so `pull_request_target` and `push` blocks are graded too |
| scoping | trigger + cancel flag | the **group itself** is the discriminator; grading every block reddened three *correct* `neomjs/neo` workflows (two cron pipelines keyed on nothing, one sweep keyed on `${{ matrix.pr }}`) |

Both count the same population here — the guard reports *15 ref-keyed blocks of 18 across 25 files*, and my audit below independently counts 15.

### Live audit at `dev@274b63beac`

`.github/workflows` is byte-identical between `origin/dev` and the tree I measured on. Parsing all 19 PR-triggered workflows:

- **15** declare `cancel-in-progress: true`, and **all 15** carry `github.run_attempt == '1' && github.ref || github.run_id`.
- **4** (`codeql-analysis`, `pr-base-guard`, `review-admission-mergeability`, `substrate-sync`) declare no `concurrency` block at all — the arm skips them, correctly, because a workflow that never cancels cannot cancel a newer head.
- **0 violations.** The restoration is coverage for a contract that currently holds, not a defect fix — worth stating so the leaf is not filed as a bug.

### The residue, because "covered" is not "fires"

The discharge is not total. Arm 1 also implied a **group-shape** obligation the guard deliberately declines: a canceling `pull_request` workflow whose group is keyed on something that is *not* the ref (a constant, or `github.workflow` alone) would red under the arm and is **skipped** by #42, which grades only groups that have declared themselves per-ref superseding groups. That is over-broad cancellation — a real defect, a different one, and out of #42's stated scope.

**At `dev` that set is empty:** every canceling PR workflow is ref-keyed. So it is a future-shape risk, not a present gap, and it does not justify restoring the arm today.

### The condition on the discharge, named rather than assumed

`neomjs/neo` already depends on `neo-agent-skills@^0.1.3` with a `neo-agent-skills-materialize` postinstall, so consumption is a small wiring change — **but the guard is not running here yet**, and #42's own body sequences the consumer-facing baseline job behind an npm release. Until that lands, this repository has **no enforcement** of the contract, only 15 workflows that happen to satisfy it.

**Discharge trigger:** #42 merges → a `neo-agent-skills` version ships → `neomjs/neo` wires `check-workflow-concurrency` into CI. If that sequence is abandoned, arm 1 returns to this ticket's owed set at full weight.

That spec covered `test.yml`'s `concurrency` block. **That guard now exists in `neomjs/neo-agent-skills` as `scripts/check-workflow-concurrency.mjs`** (skills PR #42), and its remaining work — wiring it to run for consumer repositories — is already ticketed as `neo-agent-skills#41`.

The census that finds these rows is repo-scoped by construction, so it cannot see scope that moved — which is the same blind spot this ticket documents about the split's own retirement account, pointed the other way.

**So the neo-side scope of this ticket is complete at 26 of 27**, with the 27th's coverage owned by `neo-agent-skills#41`. It asserted both that `rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs` imports nothing from `ai/**` (still true, still checkable, kept) and that the emitter carries its re-chunk pass ordered before its derive call — by reading `ai/services/github-workflow/SyncService.mjs`, which left in the split.
